key_insight: PINN-LPCDD learns physically consistent interfaces between media, enabling sharp contact discontinuities in neural simulations of compressible multi-medium flows.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets compressible-flow problems with shocks, large pressure ratios, and strong differences in material stiffness.
method: Use separate neural networks for each medium with learnable interface positions and sharp-interface coupling.
Solve Euler equations with artificial viscosity to improve robustness around shocks.
Exploit Euler-equation scaling invariance to handle high pressure ratios.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on air-air, air-helium, air-water, and air-R22 problems show acceptable accuracy according to the abstract, which reports no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: Artificial viscosity may require careful tuning to stabilize shocks without excessively smoothing flow features.
paper_title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
